Reducing Comparisons in Binary Search Tree

In the paper the author introduces two additional nodes called the candidate and sentinel nodes.

To remove testing for the null node each leaf of the tree points to the sentinel node and when a search is performed the sentinel node is given the search value. If we finish the search and end up at the sentinel value we return a not found. Otherwise we have found the value in the tree.

The candidate node is used to remove testing for greater than and equal to. The only test performed is less than. If the value is not less than then we save the current node as the candidate node and continue to the right. When the search is finished we compare the candidate node to see if it is null or the sentinel node; if not then we test to see if it holds the value we are interested in.
